title: Multiparametric senescence profiling by spectral flow cytometry uncovers endothelial heterogeneity following irradiation
task: Identify heterogeneous senescence responses in endothelial cells after radiation exposure
key_results: Dose-dependent senescence induction observed across 0-20 Gy range; higher energy X-rays (18 MV) showed greater senescence effect than 10 MV at equivalent dose rates
comments: Spectral flow cytometry with 14-color panel enables comprehensive single-cell phenotyping, though UMAP-based clustering may obscure quantitative dose-response relationships in heterogeneous populations.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Radiation dose correlates with senescence marker expression in surviving endothelial cells
hypotheses.result: Confirmed - dose-dependent response observed across both 10 and 18 MV energies

hypotheses.hypothesis: Higher energy X-rays produce greater senescence induction than lower energy at same dose
hypotheses.result: Confirmed - 18 MV showed more pronounced senescence-related effects than 10 MV

title: Effects of Yijing decoction on diminished ovarian reserve: associations with mitochondrial function, apoptosis, and the PGC-1α/SIRT3/HIF-1α pathway
task: Restore ovarian reserve function by targeting mitochondrial dysfunction and granulosa cell apoptosis
key_results: YJD treatment increased anti-Müllerian hormone levels, restored estrous cyclicity, reduced FSH/LH, and decreased granulosa cell apoptosis while preserving mitochondrial membrane potential in DOR mice
comments: The PGC-1α/SIRT3/HIF-1α pathway is identified computationally via network pharmacology but requires functional validation to establish causality rather than association.

model_io.model: Isolated granulosa cells from DOR mice

hypotheses.hypothesis: YJD compounds reduce granulosa cell apoptosis and preserve mitochondrial function in DOR
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: YJD suppressed GC apoptosis, reduced ROS, and preserved mitochondrial homeostasis

hypotheses.hypothesis: PGC-1α/SIRT3/HIF-1α pathway mediates YJD protective effects
hypotheses.result: Supported but unvalidated: YJD upregulated PGC-1α/SIRT3 and downregulated HIF-1α; causal role requires functional studies

title: Nonlinear joint modeling of oxygenation indices for dynamic mortality prediction in neonates with persistent pulmonary hypertension receiving inhaled nitric oxide
task: Mortality prediction in PPHN neonates using dynamic oxygenation indices
key_results: Nonlinear OSI-based joint model achieved validation AUC of 0.84 and 24-h AUC of 0.93, outperforming linear models (AUC 0.78-0.82), Cox models (AUC 0.74-0.79), and nSOFA (AUC 0.68-0.70)
comments: Joint modeling of longitudinal biomarkers with survival outcomes is appropriate, though external validation beyond the cohort would strengthen clinical applicability

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dynamic oxygenation indices (OSI/OI) associate with mortality better than static indices
hypotheses.result: Non-survivors showed persistently higher OSI and OI trajectories (p<0.001); nonlinear OSI model outperformed alternatives

hypotheses.hypothesis: Early OSI trajectories predict 24-h survival probability
hypotheses.result: Early trajectories strongly influenced survival probability; 24-h AUC=0.93 with time-updated predictions

title: Multi-objective sustainable DER allocation in active distribution networks based on Slime Mould Algorithm
task: Multi-objective DER placement and sizing via Slime Mould Algorithm optimization
key_results: SMA reduces active power loss 202.67→58.73 kW (71.0%), reactive loss 135.14→42.85 kVAr (68.3%), increases voltage stability index 0.6678→0.9548, cuts emissions 1.46M→0.84M kg CO₂/yr (42.1%), achieves 92.35% renewable penetration; outperforms PSO, DE, GA, WOA on convergence and robustness.
comments: Comprehensive multi-objective framework with strong empirical gains on IEEE 33-bus benchmark, but evaluation confined to single radial network; scalability to larger/meshed grids unclear.

hypotheses.hypothesis: SMA efficiently balances multiple sustainability objectives in DER optimization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: simultaneous improvements in loss, voltage, emissions, and renewable penetration; Friedman/Wilcoxon tests validate superiority.

hypotheses.hypothesis: SMA converges faster and more robustly than evolutionary algorithms (PSO, GA, DE, WOA)
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: SMA demonstrates superior convergence speed and computational efficiency across tests.

hypotheses.hypothesis: DER penetration, load variation, and objective-function weights significantly affect network performance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: sensitivity analysis shows substantial performance shifts with parameter variation.

title: Robust UAV target detection under synthetic severe weather degradations with adaptive feature propagation
task: UAV object detection under synthetic severe weather degradation
key_results: SW-DEIM achieves AP50 of 68.1% and AP50:95 of 50.0% on Drone-SW (+7.9 and +6.5pp over DEIM); AP50 of 55.8% on foggy HazyDet subset (+7.1pp); inference at 188.2 FPS.
comments: Strong synthetic benchmark results with good speed-accuracy trade-off, but authors explicitly note lack of evaluation on real rainy/snowy UAV imagery limits generalization claims.

inputs: UAV imagery under rain/fog/snow (synthetic or natural)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive feature propagation and learnable channel modulation improve multi-scale robustness under weather
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: AFPPN and DBB yield consistent AP improvements on both synthetic and real foggy data.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Degradation-oriented representations transfer to real-world foggy domain
hypotheses.result: Partially supported: transfer demonstrated on real foggy subset, but rain/snow transfer remains unvalidated.

title: Digital literacy shapes AI chatbot adoption, barriers, and performance outcomes in football coaches: a multi-method analytical study
task: AI chatbot adoption drivers among football coaches via digital literacy mediation
key_results: Digital literacy fully mediates age–adoption relationship (ab = −0.31); critical competency threshold 4.5/7 separates 28% adoption (below) from 78% (above, χ²=48.7); 'AI Value Chain' segment (10%) reports 3+ hrs/week time savings.
comments: Well-designed mediation and threshold analysis on 213 coaches, but cross-sectional design prevents causal inference and self-reported outcomes may introduce reporting bias.

outputs: user clusters including 'AI Value Chain' segment

hypotheses.hypothesis: Age negatively affects adoption; digital literacy mediates this relationship
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: age effect on adoption fully mediated (indirect only, no direct effect).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Experience-related cultural barrier is explained by lower digital literacy
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: perceived barrier among >15-year coaches fully explained by literacy deficits (ab=0.38).

hypotheses.hypothesis: A distinct high-value user segment exists with outsized satisfaction and time gains
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 10% 'AI Value Chain' cluster shows M=8.9 satisfaction vs. lower clusters (F=15.8, p<0.001).

title: Troll detection using generative adversarial network (GAN) based on social network features
task: Troll detection via GAN with behavior change simulation
key_results: TrollGAN achieves higher accuracy and F1-score than LSTM and logistic regression on Twitter datasets (14,940 labeled instances and ~3M Russian tweets); maintains stable performance at scale.
comments: Semi-supervised GAN approach is novel for trolling, but evaluation limited to Twitter domain and comparison baselines are relatively weak (no recent deep learning competitors).

model_io.model: TrollGAN (Generator + Discriminator + Classifier with shared LSTM)

hypotheses.hypothesis: GAN's adversarial framework with shared LSTM improves troll detection under behavioral drift
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: TrollGAN achieves better generalization and robustness than baselines across scale and complexity.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Social network features enhance troll identification
hypotheses.result: Supported: Method incorporates relational insights from network analysis for improved detection.

title: Inert gas atmospheric pressure plasma post-processing of fused silica micro-lenses produced by means of femtosecond laser-induced chemical etching
task: Surface roughness reduction of femtosecond laser-etched fused silica micro-lenses via atmospheric pressure plasma polishing
key_results: Surface roughness (Ra) reduced from 0.207 ± 0.044 µm to 0.047 ± 0.018 µm (>75% reduction)
Optimal parameters: 5 mm discharge gap, 5.5 W plasma power
comments: Effective post-processing method that maintains lens geometry while achieving significant surface quality improvement, though process requires careful parameter tuning to avoid plasma instability.

model_io.model: Inert gas atmospheric pressure plasma polishing
outputs: polished micro-lenses with reduced surface roughness

hypotheses.hypothesis: Plasma polishing efficiency depends on discharge gap thickness and power
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; optimum at 5 mm gap and 5.5 W with stable discharge and high electric field strength

hypotheses.hypothesis: Plasma post-processing preserves lens geometry while reducing roughness
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via microscopic and interferometric characterization
